title.zh: 卷一百四十九 列傳第七十四 劉第五班王李
title.en: Volume 149 Biographies 74: Liu, Di, five Bans, Wang, Li
title.raw: 卷一百四十九 列傳第七十四 劉第五班王李 Volume 149 Biographies 74: Liu, Di, five Bans, Wang, Li

sentences.zh: 劉第五班王李

translations.literal: Liu, Di, the five Bans, Wang, Li
translations.idiomatic: Liu, Di, the five members of the Ban family, Wang, and Li

sentences.zh: 劉晏，字士安，曹州南華人。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, style name Shi'an, was a native of Nanhua in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, whose style name was Shi'an, came from Nanhua in Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 玄宗封泰山，晏始八歲，獻頌行在，帝奇其幼，命宰相張說試之，說曰：「國瑞也。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong performed the Feng and Shan rites at Mount Tai, Yan was only eight. He presented a eulogy at the imperial encampment. The emperor marveled at his youth and ordered the chief minister Zhang Yue to test him. Yue said, "A national auspice."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong went to Mount Tai for the Feng and Shan sacrifices, Yan was only eight years old. He presented a laudatory poem at the imperial camp, and the emperor was struck by his precocity. He ordered the chief minister Zhang Yue to examine the boy. Yue declared, "This is an auspicious omen for the realm."

sentences.zh: 即授太子正字。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed Rectifier of Texts for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was immediately appointed Rectifier of Texts in the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 公卿邀請旁午，號神童，名震一時。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers invited him in unbroken succession. He was called a divine child, and his fame shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: High ministers vied to invite him, and he was hailed as a prodigy whose name resounded throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，累調夏令，未嘗督賦，而輸無逋期。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he was repeatedly transferred as magistrate of Xia. He never pressed for tax collection, yet deliveries were never overdue.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he served repeatedly as magistrate of Xia County. He never hounded the people for taxes, yet all payments arrived on time.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正，補溫令，所至有惠利可紀，民皆刻石以傳。

translations.literal: Recommended as worthy and upright, he was appointed magistrate of Wen. Wherever he went there were benefits worth recording, and the people all carved stone to spread the account.
translations.idiomatic: After he was recommended as worthy and upright, he was appointed magistrate of Wen. In every post he left tangible benefits for the people, who set up stone inscriptions to preserve his deeds.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted twice, eventually reaching the post of Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，避地襄陽。

translations.literal: When the Lushan rebellion broke out, he took refuge in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, he fled to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 永王璘署晏右職，固辭。

translations.literal: Prince of Yong Li Lin appointed Yan to a high post, but he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yong, Li Lin, offered Yan a senior appointment, but Yan steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 移書房琯，論封建與古異，「今諸王出深宮，一旦望桓、文功，不可致。」

translations.literal: He sent a letter to Fang Guan discussing how enfeoffment differed from antiquity: "Today the princes leave the deep palace and at once look to the achievements of Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi—such things cannot be attained."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Fang Guan arguing that present-day enfeoffment differed from antiquity: "The princes now leave the palace seclusion and at once expect to match the achievements of Duke Huan and Duke Wen—such ambitions cannot be realized."

sentences.zh: 詔拜度支郎中，兼侍御史，領江淮租庸事。

translations.literal: He was ordered appointed Director of the Bureau of Revenue, concurrently Attending Censor, and put in charge of the Jiang-Huai corvée and tax transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Director of the Bureau of Revenue and concurrent Attending Censor, with charge of corvée and tax transport in the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 晏至吳郡而璘反，乃與采訪使李希言謀拒之。

translations.literal: When Yan reached Wu Commandery, Lin rebelled. He then joined the Investigation Commissioner Li Xiyan in planning resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had just reached Wu Commandery when Li Lin rebelled, and he joined the investigation commissioner Li Xiyan in plotting resistance.

sentences.zh: 希言假晏守餘杭，會戰不利，走依晏。

translations.literal: Xiyan had Yan act as defender of Yuhang. When battle went badly, he fled to rely on Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiyan had Yan hold Yuhang as acting defender. When the fighting turned against them, Xiyan fled to Yan for refuge.

sentences.zh: 晏為陳可守計，因發義兵堅壁。

translations.literal: Yan set forth plans by which the city could be held and accordingly raised volunteer troops and strengthened the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yan laid out a plan for holding the city, raised local militia, and fortified the defenses.

sentences.zh: 會王敗，欲轉略州縣，聞晏有備，遂自晉陵西走。

translations.literal: When the prince was defeated and wished to turn to seize prefectures and counties, he heard that Yan was prepared and therefore withdrew west from Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was defeated and tried to seize more prefectures and counties, he learned that Yan was ready and withdrew west from Jinling.

sentences.zh: 終不言功。

translations.literal: In the end he never spoke of his merit.
translations.idiomatic: He never afterward spoke of his own achievements.

sentences.zh: 召拜彭原太守，徙隴、華二州刺史，遷河南尹。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Grand Administrator of Pengyuan, transferred as Inspector of Long and Hua prefectures, and promoted to Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and made Grand Administrator of Pengyuan, then transferred to the inspectorates of Long and Hua, and finally promoted to Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時史朝義盜東都，乃治長水。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Chaoyi was plundering the Eastern Capital, so he governed from Changshui.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Chaoyi raiding the Eastern Capital, he administered affairs from Changshui.

sentences.zh: 進戶部侍郎，兼御史中丞、度支鑄錢鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of the Household, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Commissioner for Revenue, coinage, salt, and iron.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Household and concurrently served as Censor-in-Chief and commissioner over revenue, coinage, salt, and iron.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹鄭叔清、李齊物坐殘摯罷，詔晏兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: The Intendants of Jingzhao Zheng Shuqing and Li Qiwu were dismissed for cruelty and severity, and Yan was ordered to serve concurrently as Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingzhao intendants Zheng Shuqing and Li Qiwu were removed for harsh rule, and Yan was ordered to serve concurrently as Jingzhao intendant.

sentences.zh: 總大體不苛，號稱職。

translations.literal: He grasped the broad principles without harshness and was acclaimed as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He governed by broad principles rather than petty severity and was praised as fully competent in office.

sentences.zh: 會司農卿嚴莊下獄，已而釋，誣劾晏漏禁中語，宰相蕭華亦忌之，貶通州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Minister of Agriculture Yan Zhuang was imprisoned and then released, he falsely impeached Yan for leaking palace speech. The chief minister Xiao Hua also resented him, and he was demoted to Inspector of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Minister of Agriculture Yan Zhuang was imprisoned and later released, he falsely accused Liu Yan of leaking confidential palace talk. Chief Minister Xiao Hua also bore him ill will, and Yan was demoted to inspector of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，復為京兆尹、戶部侍郎，領度支、鹽鐵、轉運、鑄錢、租庸使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended, Yan was again made Intendant of Jingzhao and Vice Minister of the Household, and put in charge of the commissioners for revenue, salt and iron, transport, coinage, and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Daizong took the throne, Yan was restored as Jingzhao intendant and Vice Minister of the Household, with charge of revenue, salt and iron, transport, coinage, and corvée.

sentences.zh: 晏以戶部讓顏真卿，改國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Yan yielded the Household Ministry to Yan Zhenqing and was changed to Rector of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Yan yielded the Ministry of the Household to Yan Zhenqing and was transferred to Rector of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 又以京兆讓嚴武，即拜吏部尚書、同中書門下平章事，使如故。

translations.literal: He also yielded Jingzhao to Yan Wu and was at once appointed Minister of the Civil Service, Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, with his commissions unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise yielded Jingzhao to Yan Wu and was immediately appointed Minister of the Civil Service and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, while retaining his existing commissions.

sentences.zh: 坐與程元振善，罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: Because of his friendship with Cheng Yuanzhen, he was removed and made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his association with Cheng Yuanzhen, he was dismissed from the council and made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 俄進御史大夫，領東都、河南、江淮轉運、租庸、鹽鐵、常平使。

translations.literal: Shortly he was advanced to Censor-in-Chief and put in charge of the transport, corvée, salt and iron, and Ever-Normal commissioners for the Eastern Capital, Henan, and Jiang-Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief and placed in charge of transport, corvée, salt and iron, and Ever-Normal granaries for the Eastern Capital, Henan, and the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 時大兵後，京師米鬥千錢，禁膳不兼時，甸農挼穗以輸。

translations.literal: At the time, after great warfare, grain in the capital cost a thousand cash per dou. Palace meals were not served on schedule, and farmers in the suburbs rubbed out the ears of grain to make delivery.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of prolonged warfare, grain in the capital sold for a thousand cash per dou. Palace meals could not be served on time, and suburban farmers stripped ears from the stalk to meet tax deliveries.

sentences.zh: 晏乃自按行，浮淮、泗，達於汴，入於河。

translations.literal: Yan then personally made an inspection tour, floating along the Huai and Si, reaching Bian, and entering the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then conducted a personal inspection, traveling by water along the Huai and Si to Bian and then into the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 右循底柱、硤石，觀三門遺跡；

translations.literal: He went right along Dizhu and Xiaoshi, viewing the traces of Sanmen;
translations.idiomatic: He followed the course past Dizhu and Xiaoshi to examine the remains of the Sanmen works;

sentences.zh: 至河陰、鞏、洛，見宇文愷梁公堰，廝河為通濟渠，視李傑新堤，盡得其病利。

translations.literal: he reached Heyin, Gong, and Luo, saw Yuwen Kai's Liang Duke weir that split the river to form the Tongji Canal, and inspected Li Jie's new embankments, fully grasping their defects and advantages.
translations.idiomatic: and reached Heyin, Gong, and Luoyang, where he studied Yuwen Kai's Liang Duke weir that diverted the river into the Tongji Canal and Li Jie's new dikes, learning every advantage and defect in the waterways.

sentences.zh: 然畏為人牽制，乃移書於宰相元載，以為：「大抵運之利與害各有四：京師三輔，苦稅入之重，淮、湖粟至，可減徭賦半，為一利；

translations.literal: Yet fearing restraint by others, he sent a letter to the chief minister Yuan Zai, stating: "Broadly speaking, transport has four benefits and four harms each. The capital and the three adjunct commanderies suffer under heavy tax deliveries. If grain from the Huai and lakes arrives, corvée and levies can be cut by half—this is the first benefit;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that others would tie his hands, he wrote to Chief Minister Yuan Zai: "Broadly speaking, canal transport has four benefits and four drawbacks. The capital and its three adjunct commanderies groan under heavy tax deliveries. If grain from the Huai region and the lakes can reach them, corvée and levies may be cut by half—this is the first benefit;

sentences.zh: 東都雕破，百戶無一存，若漕路流通，則聚落邑廛漸可還定，為二利；

translations.literal: the Eastern Capital is carved and broken, not one household in a hundred remains. If the transport route is opened, settlements and market towns can gradually be restored—this is the second benefit;
translations.idiomatic: the Eastern Capital lies in ruins, with scarcely one household in a hundred still standing. If the transport route is restored, villages and market towns can gradually be resettled—this is the second benefit;

sentences.zh: 諸將有不廷，戎虜有侵盜，聞我貢輸錯入，軍食豐衍，可以震耀夷夏，為三利；

translations.literal: when generals are disobedient and barbarians raid and plunder, hearing that our tribute transport arrives in steady flow and army provisions abound can awe both Chinese and foreigners—this is the third benefit;
translations.idiomatic: when generals defy the court or barbarians raid the borders, the knowledge that tribute grain is flowing in steadily and army provisions are ample can overawe both Chinese and foreigners—this is the third benefit;

sentences.zh: 若舟車既通，百貨雜集，航海梯嶠，可追貞觀、永徽之盛，為四利。

translations.literal: if boats and carts are connected and all goods gather, with sea voyages and mountain ladders, the prosperity of the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras can be approached—this is the fourth benefit.
translations.idiomatic: once boats and carts are linked and goods of every kind converge, with trade by sea and over mountain passes, the prosperity of the Zhenguan and Yonghui reigns may be approached again—this is the fourth benefit.

sentences.zh: 起宜陽、熊耳，虎牢、成臯五百里，見戶才千餘，居無尺椽，爨無盛煙，獸遊鬼哭，而使轉車免漕，功且難就，為一病；

translations.literal: From Yiyang and Xiong'er to Hulao and Chenggao, five hundred li, visible households number only a little over a thousand. Dwellings have not a foot of rafter, cooking fires show no heavy smoke, beasts roam and ghosts weep—yet to make relay carts replace canal transport, the task will be hard to complete. This is the first harm;
translations.idiomatic: From Yiyang and Xiong'er to Hulao and Chenggao, a stretch of five hundred li holds barely a thousand visible households. Homes lack even a foot of timber, hearths show scarcely a wisp of smoke, and beasts roam where ghosts might wail—yet to replace canal transport with relay carts in such a land would be nearly impossible. This is the first drawback;

sentences.zh: 河、汴自寇難以來，不復穿治，崩岸滅木，所在廞淤，涉泗千里，如罔水行舟，為二病；

translations.literal: the Yellow River and Bian Canal since the troubles of rebellion have not been dredged. Collapsed banks and drowned trees silt up everywhere. Crossing the Si for a thousand li is like sailing a boat in a net—this is the second harm;
translations.idiomatic: since the rebellions the Yellow River and Bian Canal have gone unrepaired. Collapsed banks and drowned timber have silted the channels everywhere, so that a thousand-li passage along the Si is like steering a boat through a net—this is the second drawback;

sentences.zh: 東垣、底柱，澠池、北河之間六百里，戍邏久絕，奪攘奸宄，夾河為藪，為三病；

translations.literal: between Dongyuan and Dizhu, Chi and the north of the river, six hundred li, garrison patrols have long ceased. Robbery and treachery fill the banks on both sides of the river—this is the third harm;
translations.idiomatic: along the six hundred li between Dongyuan and Dizhu, from Chi to the north bank, frontier patrols have long ceased. Brigands and rebels hold both banks of the river—this is the third drawback;

sentences.zh: 淮陰去蒲阪，亙三千里，屯壁相望，中軍皆鼎司元侯，每言衣無纊，食半菽，免漕所至，輒留以饋軍，非單車使者折簡書所能制，為四病。」

translations.literal: From Huaiyin to Puban stretches three thousand li. Fortified camps face one another. The central armies are all chief ministers and great marquises. Each says they lack padded garments and eat half beans. Wherever canal exemption reaches, they at once detain it to feed the army. This is not something a lone envoy with a folded letter can control—this is the fourth harm."
translations.idiomatic: From Huaiyin to Puban stretches three thousand li of garrisons facing one another. The central armies are commanded by chief ministers and great feudatories who constantly plead that they lack padded clothing and eat half beans. Wherever canal grain arrives, they seize it for their troops. No lone envoy bearing a folded dispatch can restrain them—this is the fourth drawback."

sentences.zh: 載方內擅朝權，既得書，即盡以漕事委晏，故晏得盡其才。

translations.literal: Zai was then monopolizing court power inwardly. Once he received the letter, he entrusted all canal affairs to Yan, and so Yan was able to display his full talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai was then monopolizing court power. Once he received the letter, he entrusted all canal transport to Yan, who was thus able to bring his full abilities to bear.

sentences.zh: 歲輸始至，天子大悅，遣衛士以鼓吹迓東渭橋，馳使勞曰：「卿，朕酂侯也。」

translations.literal: When the year's transport first arrived, the Son of Heaven was greatly pleased. He sent guards with music to welcome him at the Eastern Wei Bridge and dispatched a fast messenger to console him, saying, "Minister, you are my Marquis of Zan."
translations.idiomatic: When the first annual shipment arrived, the emperor was overjoyed. He sent guards with ceremonial music to welcome Yan at the Eastern Wei Bridge and dispatched a fast courier with words of praise: "Minister, you are my Marquis of Zan."

sentences.zh: 凡歲致四十萬斛，自是關中雖水旱，物不翔貴矣。

translations.literal: In all, forty myriads of hu were delivered each year. From then on, although Guanzhong suffered flood or drought, prices did not soar.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he delivered four hundred thousand hu of grain, and thereafter, even when Guanzhong suffered flood or drought, prices no longer soared.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏部尚書，又兼益湖南、荊南、山南東道轉運、常平、鑄錢使，與第五琦分領天下金谷。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Minister of the Civil Service and also put in charge of the transport, Ever-Normal, and coinage commissioners for Yizhou, Hunan, Jingnan, and Shannan East Circuit, dividing control of the realm's revenue with Di Wuqi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Minister of the Civil Service and also given charge of transport, Ever-Normal granaries, and coinage for Yizhou, Hunan, Jingnan, and Shannan East Circuit, sharing control of the empire's finances with Di Wuqi.

sentences.zh: 又知吏部三銓事，推處最殿分明，下皆慴伏。

translations.literal: He also managed the three selection boards of the Civil Service Ministry. His promotions and demotions were clearest in rank, and subordinates all submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He also oversaw the three selection boards of the Ministry of the Civil Service. His rankings of candidates were unmistakably clear, and all subordinates submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 元載得罪，詔晏鞫之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai was found guilty, Yan was ordered to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai was condemned, the court ordered Yan to conduct the interrogation.

sentences.zh: 晏畏載黨盛，不敢獨訊，更敕李涵等五人與晏雜治。

translations.literal: Yan feared Zai's faction was strong and dared not examine alone. He was further ordered that Li Han and five others should join Yan in mixed handling.
translations.idiomatic: Yan feared Zai's faction was too powerful to interrogate alone and asked that Li Han and four others join him in the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 王縉得免死，晏請之也。

translations.literal: Wang Jin was spared death—it was Yan who pleaded for him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin was spared execution at Yan's intercession.

sentences.zh: 常袞執政，忌晏有公望，乃言晏舊德，當師長百僚，用為左僕射，實欲奪其權。

translations.literal: Chang Gun held power and resented Yan's public esteem. He said Yan's old virtue should make him leader of the hundred officials and appointed him Left Vice Director, in truth intending to strip his authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Gun held power, he resented Yan's public standing. Praising Yan's long service, he argued that Yan should head the bureaucracy and appointed him Left Vice Director—an honor meant in fact to strip him of real authority.

sentences.zh: 帝以計務方治，詔以僕射領使如舊。

translations.literal: The emperor, because fiscal affairs were then being managed, ordered that as Vice Director he should lead the commissions as before.
translations.idiomatic: Because fiscal affairs were still urgent, the emperor ordered that Yan retain his commissions as before despite the vice directorship.

sentences.zh: 初，晏分置諸道租庸使，慎簡臺閣士專之。

translations.literal: At first Yan established corvée commissioners in each circuit and carefully selected men from the central offices to specialize in the work.
translations.idiomatic: From the outset Yan established corvée commissioners in each circuit and carefully chose specialists from the central bureaucracy to staff them.

sentences.zh: 時經費不充，停天下攝官，獨租庸得補署，積數百人，皆新進銳敏，盡當時之選，趣督倚辦，故能成功。

translations.literal: At the time funds were insufficient and acting officials throughout the realm were suspended. Only the corvée offices could make supplemental appointments. Several hundred were accumulated, all newly advanced, sharp and keen—the choicest of the age. They hastened supervision and relied on execution, and so success was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Funds were then scarce and acting officials were suspended empire-wide, but the corvée offices alone could make supplemental appointments. Yan gathered several hundred of the sharpest new men available, pressed them into urgent service, and thereby achieved success.

sentences.zh: 雖權貴幹請，欲假職仕者，晏厚以稟入奉之，然未嘗使親事，是以人人勸職。

translations.literal: Although powerful men made requests and wished to borrow posts for employment, Yan richly supplied them from incoming revenue, yet never let them handle affairs in person. Therefore everyone was encouraged in duty.
translations.idiomatic: When powerful men sought posts for their clients, Yan paid them generously from incoming revenue but never let them handle real business, so that everyone else was driven to perform their duties.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「士有爵祿，則名重於利；

translations.literal: He once said: "When scholars have rank and salary, then reputation weighs heavier than profit;
translations.idiomatic: He once remarked, "When a gentleman holds rank and stipend, reputation outweighs profit;

sentences.zh: 吏無榮進，則利重於名。」

translations.literal: when clerks have no honorable advancement, then profit weighs heavier than reputation."
translations.idiomatic: but when a clerk has no prospect of honorable advancement, profit outweighs reputation."

sentences.zh: 故檢劾出納，一委士人，吏惟奉行文書而已。

translations.literal: Therefore inspection of receipts and disbursements was entirely entrusted to scholars; clerks only carried out documents.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly he entrusted all auditing of receipts and disbursements to educated officials, while clerks merely executed the paperwork.

sentences.zh: 所任者，雖數千里外，奉教令如目前，頻伸諧戲不敢隱。

translations.literal: Those appointed, though several thousand li away, obeyed instructions as if before their eyes. They frequently reported and jested and did not dare conceal.
translations.idiomatic: Those he appointed, though thousands of li distant, obeyed his orders as if he stood before them, reporting frankly and withholding nothing.

sentences.zh: 惟晏能行之，它人不能也。

translations.literal: Only Yan could carry this out; others could not.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yan could operate in this way; no one else could match him.

sentences.zh: 代宗嘗命考所部官吏善惡，刺史有罪者，五品以上輒系劾，六品以下杖然後奏。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong once ordered him to assess the good and evil of officials under his jurisdiction. When prefects were guilty, fifth rank and above were at once bound and impeached; sixth rank and below were beaten and then reported.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong once ordered him to evaluate officials under his jurisdiction. Prefects found guilty at fifth rank or above were immediately arrested and impeached; those of sixth rank or below were beaten first and then reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 李靈耀反，河南節帥或不奉法，擅征賦，州縣益削。

translations.literal: When Li Lingyao rebelled, the military commissioners of Henan sometimes did not obey the law and levied taxes on their own authority, and prefectures and counties grew ever weaker.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled, some Henan military commissioners ignored the law and levied taxes on their own authority, further weakening prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 晏常以羨補乏，人不加調，而所入自如。

translations.literal: Yan constantly used surplus to supply deficiency. The people were not subjected to added levies, yet revenue remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yan constantly used surpluses from one region to cover shortages in another, so that the people faced no added levies while revenue remained steady.

sentences.zh: 第五琦始榷鹽佐軍興，晏代之，法益密，利無遺入。

translations.literal: Di Wuqi first monopolized salt to assist military expansion. Yan replaced him, and the law grew stricter so that profit left nothing uncollected.
translations.idiomatic: Di Wuqi had first imposed the salt monopoly to fund the armies. Yan succeeded him and tightened the system until every possible profit was captured.

sentences.zh: 初，歲收緡錢六十萬，末乃什之，計歲入千二百萬，而榷居太半，民不告勤。

translations.literal: At first annual collection of cash was six hundred thousand strings. In the end it was increased tenfold, totaling twelve million strings annually, of which the monopoly supplied the greater part, yet the people did not complain of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: At first annual cash receipts were six hundred thousand strings; eventually he increased them tenfold to twelve million, with the salt monopoly supplying more than half, yet the people did not complain of undue burden.

sentences.zh: 京師鹽暴貴，詔取三萬斛以贍關中，自揚州四旬至都，人以為神。

translations.literal: When salt in the capital suddenly became costly, he was ordered to take thirty thousand hu to supply Guanzhong. From Yangzhou to the capital in forty days, people considered it miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: When salt prices in the capital soared, he was ordered to deliver thirty thousand hu to supply Guanzhong. The shipment reached the capital from Yangzhou in forty days, and the people regarded it as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 至湖嶠荒險處，所出貨皆賤弱，不償所轉，晏悉儲淮、楚間，貿銅易薪，歲鑄緡錢十餘萬。

translations.literal: In remote and perilous lake and mountain regions, goods produced were all cheap and weak and did not repay transport costs. Yan stored them all between the Huai and Chu, traded copper for fuel, and annually cast more than a hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In remote lake and mountain districts the local goods were too cheap to justify transport costs. Yan stockpiled them between the Huai and Chu, traded copper for fuel, and annually cast more than a hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 其措置纖悉如此。

translations.literal: His arrangements were as meticulous as this.
translations.idiomatic: His arrangements were meticulous in this fashion throughout.

sentences.zh: 諸道巡院，皆募駛足，置驛相望，四方貨殖低昂及它利害，雖甚遠，不數日即知，是能權萬貨重輕，使天下無甚貴賤而物常平，自言如見錢流地上。

translations.literal: In the inspection offices of each circuit he recruited swift runners and set relay stations facing one another. The rise and fall of goods in the four directions and other advantages and harms, though very distant, were known within a few days. Thus he could weigh the heavy and light of ten thousand goods and keep the realm without great cheapness or dearness so that things were constantly level. He said himself it was like seeing money flow on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: In each circuit's inspection offices he hired swift couriers and set relay stations at intervals, so that price movements and market conditions even in distant regions were known within days. He could thereby regulate the weight of every commodity and keep prices level across the empire, saying that he could see money flowing over the ground.

sentences.zh: 每朝謁，馬上以鞭算。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended court audience, he calculated on horseback with his whip.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to court each morning he worked figures with his riding crop as he rode.

sentences.zh: 質明視事，至夜分止，雖休澣不廢。

translations.literal: At dawn he handled affairs and did not stop until midnight, and even on rest days he did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: He began work at dawn and did not stop until midnight, and even on his days off he kept at it.

sentences.zh: 事無閑劇，即日剖決無留。

translations.literal: Whether affairs were minor or major, he decided them the same day without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a matter was trivial or urgent, he settled it the same day without backlog.

sentences.zh: 所居修行裏，粗樸庳陋，飲食儉狹，室無媵婢。

translations.literal: His residence in Xiuxing Lane was crude, plain, low, and shabby. His food and drink were frugal and narrow. His rooms had no concubines or maids.
translations.idiomatic: His home in Xiuxing Lane was plain and shabby, his meals frugal, and his household kept no concubines or serving women.

sentences.zh: 然任職久，勢軋宰相，要官華使多出其門。

translations.literal: Yet having served long, his power pressed upon the chief ministers, and many key posts and splendid envoys came from his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after long service his power rivaled that of the chief ministers, and many key posts and distinguished envoys came from his patronage.

sentences.zh: 自江淮茗橘珍甘，常與本道分貢，競欲先至，雖封山斷道，以禁前發，晏厚貲致之，常冠諸府，由是冒怨益多。

translations.literal: From the Jiang-Huai region, famous tea, tangerines, and rare sweets were often divided for tribute with the home circuit. All competed to arrive first. Though mountains were sealed and roads cut to forbid early dispatch, Yan paid heavily to obtain them and constantly led all prefectures. Because of this, resentment grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Fine tea, tangerines, and delicacies from the Jiang-Huai were often shared as tribute with local circuits, each striving to arrive first. Though mountains were closed and roads blocked to prevent early shipment, Yan paid lavishly to secure the finest goods and consistently outdid every other prefecture, provoking ever more resentment.

sentences.zh: 饋謝四方有名士無不至，其有口舌者，率以利啖之，使不得有所訾短。

translations.literal: Gifts and thanks reached famous scholars of the four directions without exception. Those with tongues for criticism were generally fed with profit so they could not find fault.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished gifts on renowned scholars throughout the realm, and those inclined to criticize him were usually bought off with profit so they could find no fault.

sentences.zh: 故議者頗言晏任數固恩。

translations.literal: Therefore critics often said Yan relied on stratagem to secure favor.
translations.idiomatic: Critics therefore often said that Yan relied on manipulation to secure imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 大歷時政因循，軍國皆仰晏，未嘗檢質。

translations.literal: In the Dali era government followed inertia. Army and state all depended on Yan, and he was never examined or verified.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign government drifted along inertia, and both army and state depended on Yan without anyone auditing his accounts.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，言者屢請罷轉運使，晏亦固辭，不許。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong ascended, speakers repeatedly requested abolition of the transport commissioner. Yan also firmly declined, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, critics repeatedly called for abolishing the transport commission, and Yan himself repeatedly asked to resign, but neither request was granted.

sentences.zh: 又加關內河東三川轉運、鹽鐵及諸道青苗使。

translations.literal: He was further given charge of transport and salt and iron for Guannei, Hedong, and the Three Rivers, and of the green-sprout commissioner in each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was further given charge of transport and salt and iron for Guannei, Hedong, and the Three Rivers circuits, as well as the green-sprout tax in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 始，楊炎為吏部侍郎，晏為尚書，盛氣不相下。

translations.literal: At first Yang Yan was Vice Minister of the Civil Service while Yan was Minister. Each was overbearing and would not yield to the other.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Yan had been Vice Minister of the Civil Service while Yan was Minister, and the two clashed in mutual arrogance.

sentences.zh: 晏治元載罪，而炎坐貶。

translations.literal: Yan handled Yuan Zai's crime, and Yan was demoted as a consequence.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan prosecuted Yuan Zai's crimes, Yang Yan was demoted as a collateral victim.

sentences.zh: 及炎執政，銜宿怒，將為載報仇。

translations.literal: When Yan came to power, he harbored old anger and intended to avenge Zai.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan came to power, he nursed his old grievance and set out to avenge Yuan Zai.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝居東宮，代宗寵獨孤妃，而愛其子韓王。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor resided in the Eastern Palace, Daizong favored Consort Dugu and loved her son the Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the emperor was still heir apparent, Daizong favored Consort Dugu and doted on her son, the Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 宦人劉清潭與嬖幸請立妃為後，且言王數有符異，以搖東宮。

translations.literal: The eunuch Liu Qingtan and favored attendants requested establishing the consort as empress and also said the prince repeatedly showed portents and wonders to shake the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liu Qingtan and other favorites urged that the consort be made empress and claimed that the prince showed repeated supernatural signs meant to unsettle the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 時妄言晏與謀。

translations.literal: At the time it was falsely said that Yan joined in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors then falsely implicated Liu Yan in the intrigue.

sentences.zh: 至是，炎見帝流涕曰：「賴祖宗神靈，先帝與陛下不為賊臣所間，不然，劉晏、黎幹搖動社稷，兇謀果矣。

translations.literal: At this point Yan, meeting the emperor, wept and said: "Thanks to the spirits of the ancestors, the late emperor and Your Majesty were not estranged by treacherous ministers. Otherwise Liu Yan and Li Gan would have shaken the altars of state, and the wicked plot would have succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yang Yan appeared before the emperor in tears and said, "Thanks to the spirits of our ancestors, the late emperor and Your Majesty were not turned against each other by traitorous ministers. Otherwise Liu Yan and Li Gan would have shaken the throne, and their wicked plot would have succeeded.

sentences.zh: 今幹伏辜而晏在，臣位宰相，不能正其罪，法當死。」

translations.literal: Now Gan has paid guilt while Yan remains. I hold the post of chief minister yet cannot rectify his crime. By law I should die."
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan has paid for his crimes, but Liu Yan still lives. I hold the post of chief minister yet cannot bring him to justice. By law I deserve death myself.

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫曰：「陛下已廓然大赦，不當究飛語，致人於罪。」

translations.literal: Cui Youfu said: "Your Majesty has already proclaimed a great amnesty. You should not pursue flying rumors and bring men to guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu objected, "Your Majesty has already proclaimed a great amnesty. You must not pursue idle rumors and condemn men on their basis."

sentences.zh: 朱泚、崔寧力相解釋，寧尤切至。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci and Cui Ning strongly joined in explanation, and Ning was especially earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci and Cui Ning strongly pleaded on Yan's behalf, Cui Ning most urgently of all.

sentences.zh: 炎怒，斥寧於外，遂罷晏使。

translations.literal: Yan was angry, expelled Ning to the outer circuits, and then removed Yan's commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan in anger had Cui Ning sent away from court and then stripped Liu Yan of his commissions.

sentences.zh: 坐新故所交簿物抗謬，貶忠州刺史，中官護送。

translations.literal: Because of errors in old and new account books of his associates, he was demoted to Inspector of Zhong Prefecture, with eunuchs escorting him.
translations.idiomatic: On charges of irregularities in the account books of his associates, he was demoted to inspector of Zhong Prefecture under escort by palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 炎必欲傅其罪，知庾準與晏素憾，乃擢為荊南節度使。

translations.literal: Yan was determined to attach guilt to him. Knowing Yu Zhun had long resented Yan, he promoted him to Military Commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan was determined to fix guilt upon him. Knowing that Yu Zhun had long borne a grudge against Yan, he promoted Yu to military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 準即奏晏與朱泚書，語言怨望，又搜卒，擅取官物，脅詔使，謀作亂。

translations.literal: Zhun at once memorialized that Yan had written to Zhu Ci with language of resentment, also searched out soldiers, seized official goods on his own authority, coerced imperial envoys, and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhun immediately memorialized that Yan had written to Zhu Ci in resentful language, had illegally impressed soldiers, seized government property, intimidated imperial envoys, and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 炎證成之。

translations.literal: Yan verified and completed the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan confirmed the charges.

sentences.zh: 建中元年七月，詔中人賜晏死，年六十五。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Jianzhong, an edict ordered a eunuch to grant Yan death. He was sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Jianzhong, an edict ordered a palace eunuch to grant Liu Yan death by imperial command. He was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 後十九日，賜死詔書乃下，且暴其罪。

translations.literal: Nineteen days later the edict of granted death was issued, and his crimes were also exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen days later the formal edict ordering his death was issued, publicly listing his crimes.

sentences.zh: 家屬徙嶺表，坐累者數十人，天下以為冤。

translations.literal: His family was banished to the Lingnan region. Several tens were implicated. All under Heaven considered it injustice.
translations.idiomatic: His family was exiled to the far south, and dozens of associates were implicated. The empire regarded it as a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 時炎兼刪定使，議籍沒，眾論不可，乃止。

translations.literal: At the time Yan also served as commissioner for editorial revision. They discussed confiscation of property, but public opinion would not allow it, and so they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan, who also served as commissioner for editorial revision, proposed confiscating Yan's property, but public opinion would not allow it and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 然已命簿錄其家，唯雜書兩乘，米麥數斛，人服其廉。

translations.literal: Yet they had already ordered registers of his household. There were only two cartloads of miscellaneous books and several hu of rice and wheat. People admired his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: An inventory of his household had already been ordered, however, and turned up only two cartloads of miscellaneous books and a few hu of grain. All admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 淄青節度使李正己表誅晏太暴，不加驗實，先誅後詔，天下駭惋，請還其妻子。

translations.literal: The Military Commissioner of Ziqing Li Zhengyi memorialized that executing Yan was too violent, without verification of facts, executing before the edict. All under Heaven were shocked and grieved and requested return of his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengyi, military commissioner of Ziqing, memorialized that Yan's execution had been too brutal—carried out without verification, the sentence pronounced before the edict was issued. The empire was shocked and grieved, and many petitioned for the return of his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 興元初，帝浸寤，乃許歸葬。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Xingyuan, the emperor gradually came to his senses and then permitted return for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xingyuan reign the emperor gradually came to his senses and permitted Yan's remains to be brought home for burial.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，遂擢晏子執經為太常博士，宗經秘書郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan, Yan's son Zhijing was then promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices and Zongjing to Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan, Yan's son Zhijing was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices and Zongjing was made a secretary.

sentences.zh: 執經還官，求追命，有詔贈鄭州刺史，又加司徒。

translations.literal: When Zhijing returned to office, he requested posthumous honors. There was an edict granting Yan the post of Inspector of Zheng Prefecture, and he was further given Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhijing returned to office he petitioned for posthumous honors for his father. An edict granted Liu Yan the title of Inspector of Zheng Prefecture and further elevated him to Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 晏歿二十年，而韓洄、元琇、裴腆、李衡、包佶、盧徵、李若初繼掌財利，皆晏所辟用，有名於時。

translations.literal: Twenty years after Yan's death, Han Hui, Yuan Xiu, Pei Tian, Li Heng, Bao Gu, Lu Zheng, and Li Ruochu succeeded in managing revenue, all men Yan had recruited and employed, famous in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years after Yan's death, Han Hui, Yuan Xiu, Pei Tian, Li Heng, Bao Gu, Lu Zheng, and Li Ruochu in turn managed the empire's finances—all men Yan had recruited and all renowned in their day.

sentences.zh: 晏既被誣，而舊吏推明其功。

translations.literal: After Yan was falsely accused, his former subordinates set forth and clarified his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan was falsely condemned, his former subordinates came forward to clarify his achievements.

sentences.zh: 陳諫以為管、蕭之亞，著論紀其詳，大略以「開元、天寶間天下戶千萬，至德後殘於大兵，饑疫相仍，十耗其九，至晏充使，戶不二百萬。

translations.literal: Chen Jian considered him second only to Guan Zhong and Xiao He and wrote a treatise recording the details in full. Broadly it said: "Between the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras households in the realm numbered ten million. After the Zhide reign they were ravaged by great warfare, famine and pestilence following one another, nine-tenths lost. When Yan filled the commission, households were not two million.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jian ranked him alongside Guan Zhong and Xiao He and wrote a detailed treatise on his career, noting in summary that "during the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns the empire held ten million households, but after the Zhide era warfare, famine, and pestilence in succession destroyed nine-tenths of them, so that when Yan took office fewer than two million households remained.

sentences.zh: 晏通計天下經費，謹察州縣災害，蠲除振救，不使流離死亡。

translations.literal: Yan comprehensively calculated the realm's expenditures, carefully observed disasters in prefectures and counties, remitted and relieved, and did not allow wandering exile and death.
translations.idiomatic: Yan calculated the empire's total expenditures, carefully monitored disasters in every prefecture and county, and remitted taxes and provided relief so that the people were not driven to wander and die.

sentences.zh: 初，州縣取富人督漕免，謂之『船頭』；

translations.literal: At first prefectures and counties took wealthy men to supervise canal transport exemption, calling them "boat heads";
translations.idiomatic: Previously prefectures and counties had pressed wealthy men to supervise canal transport in lieu of tax, calling them "boat heads";

sentences.zh: 主郵遞，謂之『捉驛』；

translations.literal: those who managed postal relay were called "relay catchers";
translations.idiomatic: those who managed postal relays were called "relay catchers";

sentences.zh: 稅外橫取，謂之『白著』。

translations.literal: extralegal levies beyond the tax quota were called "naked exactions."
translations.idiomatic: and extralegal levies beyond the tax quota were called "naked exactions."

sentences.zh: 人不堪命，皆去為盜賊。

translations.literal: The people could not bear their lives and all left to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The people could not endure such burdens and fled to become bandits.

sentences.zh: 上元、寶應間，如袁晁、陳莊、方清、許欽等亂江淮，十餘年乃定。

translations.literal: Between the Shangyuan and Baoying eras, men such as Yuan Chao, Chen Zhuang, Fang Qing, and Xu Qin disturbed the Jiang-Huai, and more than ten years passed before order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Shangyuan and Baoying reigns rebels such as Yuan Chao, Chen Zhuang, Fang Qing, and Xu Qin ravaged the Jiang-Huai region, and more than a decade passed before order was restored.

sentences.zh: 晏始以官船漕，而吏主驛事，罷無名之斂，正鹽官法，以裨用度。

translations.literal: Yan first used official boats for canal transport while clerks managed relay affairs, abolished nameless levies, rectified the salt monopoly law, and thereby supplemented state expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Yan first used official transport vessels and put clerks in charge of relay stations, abolished unauthorized levies, reformed the salt monopoly, and thereby supplemented state revenue.

sentences.zh: 起廣德二年，盡建中元年，黜陟使實天下戶，收三百餘萬。

translations.literal: From the second year of Guangde through the first year of Jianzhong, promotion-and-demotion commissioners verified households throughout the realm and registered more than three million.
translations.idiomatic: From the second year of Guangde through the first year of Jianzhong, promotion-and-demotion commissioners verified households empire-wide and registered more than three million.

sentences.zh: 王者愛人，不在賜與，當使之耕耘織纴，常歲平斂之，荒年蠲救之，大率歲增十之一。

translations.literal: A king who loves the people does not lie in gifts and grants. He should make them plow and weave. In normal years he levies evenly; in famine years he remits and relieves. On the whole each year increases by one-tenth.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who truly loves his people does not merely bestow gifts but ensures that they plow and weave. In normal years he levies taxes evenly; in famine years he remits and relieves. On average revenue increased by one-tenth each year.

sentences.zh: 而晏尤能時其緩急而先後之。

translations.literal: Yet Yan was especially able to time urgency and ease and put them in order of priority.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was especially skilled at timing relief according to urgency and priority.

sentences.zh: 每州縣荒歉有端，則計官所贏，先令曰：『蠲某物，貸某戶。』

translations.literal: Whenever famine and shortage in a prefecture or county had a clear cause, he calculated the surplus in the official accounts and first issued orders saying, "Remit such-and-such item, lend to such-and-such household."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a prefecture or county showed signs of famine, he calculated official surpluses and issued orders in advance: "Remit such-and-such tax; lend to such-and-such household."

sentences.zh: 民未及困，而奏報已行矣。

translations.literal: Before the people had yet reached distress, the memorial report was already carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Relief was implemented before the people had yet reached distress.

sentences.zh: 議者或譏晏不直賑救，而多賤出以濟民者，則又不然。

translations.literal: Some critics mocked Yan for not directly distributing relief but instead selling cheaply to aid the people—yet this too was mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Some critics mocked Yan for not distributing relief directly but instead selling goods cheaply to aid the people—yet this criticism too was mistaken.

sentences.zh: 善治病者，不使至危憊；

translations.literal: One skilled in treating illness does not let the patient reach critical exhaustion;
translations.idiomatic: A skilled physician does not wait until the patient is critically exhausted;

sentences.zh: 善救災者，勿使至賑給。

translations.literal: one skilled in relieving disaster does not let matters reach the point of relief distribution.
translations.idiomatic: and one skilled at disaster relief does not wait until relief distribution becomes necessary.

sentences.zh: 故賑給少則不足活人，活人多則闕國用，國用闕則復重斂矣；

translations.literal: Therefore if relief distribution is too little it is insufficient to save lives; if too many are saved state funds are depleted; when state funds are depleted heavy levies are imposed again;
translations.idiomatic: If relief is too little, it cannot save enough lives; if too much is given, state funds are depleted; and when state funds run short, heavy levies are imposed again.

sentences.zh: 又賑給近僥幸，吏下為奸，強得之多，弱得之少，雖刀鋸在前不可禁。

translations.literal: furthermore relief distribution invites opportunism, and subordinate clerks commit fraud—the strong obtain more, the weak obtain less—even with blade and saw before them it cannot be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover relief distribution invites opportunism and clerical fraud—the strong seize more, the weak receive less—and even the threat of execution cannot stop it.

sentences.zh: 以為二害。

translations.literal: These were considered two harms.
translations.idiomatic: These were considered two harms of direct relief.

sentences.zh: 災沴之鄉，所乏糧耳，它產尚在，賤以出之，易其雜貨，因人之力，轉於豐處，或官自用，則國計不乏；

translations.literal: In districts stricken by calamity what is lacking is only grain; other products remain. Sell cheaply to release them, exchange for miscellaneous goods, rely on human effort to transfer to abundant regions, or the government uses them itself—then state accounts are not depleted;
translations.idiomatic: In disaster-stricken districts grain alone is lacking while other goods remain. Sell them cheaply, exchange them for miscellaneous goods, rely on local effort to transfer them to abundant regions, or let the government use them directly—then state accounts are not depleted;

sentences.zh: 多出菽粟，恣之糶運，散入村閭，下戶力農，不能詣市，轉相沾逮，自免阻饑，不待令驅。

translations.literal: release much beans and millet, allow free sale and transport, scatter into villages and hamlets. Lower households laboring in farming cannot reach the market, yet through mutual contact they are reached and themselves escape blocked famine without waiting for orders to drive them.
translations.idiomatic: release beans and millet for free sale and transport into villages and hamlets, where farming households unable to reach markets receive grain through local exchange and thereby escape famine without waiting for official orders.

sentences.zh: 以為二勝。

translations.literal: These were considered two victories.
translations.idiomatic: These were considered two advantages of Yan's method.

sentences.zh: 晏又以常平法，豐則貴取，饑則賤與，率諸州米嘗儲三百萬斛。

translations.literal: Yan also used the Ever-Normal method: in abundance buy at high price, in famine sell at low price. On average the prefectures stored three million hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Yan also applied the Ever-Normal granary system, buying at high prices in years of plenty and selling cheaply in famine years, so that prefectures on average stored three million hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 豈所謂有功於國者邪！」

translations.literal: Was this not what is called having merit for the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Was this not service worthy of a statesman!"

sentences.zh: 琇後以尚書右丞判度支，國無橫斂而軍旅濟。

translations.literal: Xiu later served as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat judging the Bureau of Revenue. The state had no extralegal levies yet the armies were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu later served as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat with charge of the Bureau of Revenue, maintaining the realm without extralegal levies while keeping the armies supplied.

sentences.zh: 為韓滉所惡，貶雷州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He was hated by Han Huang and demoted to Revenue Adjutant of Lei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang bore him ill will and had him demoted to revenue adjutant of Lei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐私入廣州，賜死。

translations.literal: Because of entering Guangzhou privately, he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: He was sentenced to death by imperial command for entering Guangzhou without authorization.

sentences.zh: 腆以兵部侍郎判度支，封聞喜縣公。

translations.literal: Tian served as Vice Minister of War judging the Bureau of Revenue and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tian served as Vice Minister of War with charge of the Bureau of Revenue and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County.

sentences.zh: 衡歷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Heng served successively as Vice Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng rose to Vice Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 佶字幼正，潤州延陵人。

translations.literal: Gu, style name Youzheng, was a native of Yanling in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Gu, whose style name was Youzheng, came from Yanling in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父融，集賢院學士，與賀知章、張旭、張若虛有名當時，號「吳中四士」。

translations.literal: His father Rong was a scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. With He Zhizhang, Zhang Xu, and Zhang Ruoxu he was famous in the age and called "the Four Scholars of Wu."
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao Rong was a scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and, together with He Zhizhang, Zhang Xu, and Zhang Ruoxu, was famed in his day as one of the "Four Scholars of Wu."

sentences.zh: 佶擢進士第，累官諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Gu passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Gu passed the jinshi examination and rose to the post of Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 坐善元載，貶嶺南。

translations.literal: Because of his friendship with Yuan Zai, he was demoted to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his association with Yuan Zai, he was demoted to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 晏奏起為汴東兩稅使。

translations.literal: Yan memorialized to restore him as Commissioner for the Two Taxes east of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan memorialized to recall him as commissioner for the two-tax system east of Bian.

sentences.zh: 晏罷，以佶充諸道鹽鐵輕貨錢物使，遷刑部侍郎，改秘書監，封丹陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Yan was removed, Gu was made Commissioner for Salt, Iron, and Light Goods in each circuit, promoted to Vice Minister of Justice, changed to Director of the Palace Library, and enfeoffed as Duke of Danyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was dismissed, Bao Gu was appointed commissioner for salt, iron, and light goods in every circuit, promoted to Vice Minister of Justice, then made Director of the Palace Library and enfeoffed as Duke of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 徵，幽州人。

translations.literal: Zheng was a man of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zheng was a native of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 晏薦為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Yan recommended him as Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan recommended him as palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 晏得罪，貶珍州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: When Yan was found guilty, he was demoted to Revenue Adjutant of Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was condemned, Lu Zheng was demoted to revenue adjutant of Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元琇判度支，薦為員外郎。

translations.literal: When Yuan Xiu judged the Bureau of Revenue, he recommended him as Outside Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xiu took charge of the Bureau of Revenue, he recommended Lu Zheng as an outside director.

sentences.zh: 琇得罪，貶秀州長史，三遷給事中。

translations.literal: When Xiu was found guilty, he was demoted to Chief Administrator of Xiu Prefecture and was thrice promoted to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xiu was condemned, Lu Zheng was demoted to chief administrator of Xiu Prefecture but was later promoted three times to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎竇參善之，方倚以代己，會同州刺史缺，參請用尚書左丞趙憬，德宗惡參，欲間其腹心，更用徵為之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Household Dou Can favored him and was about to rely on him to replace himself. When the Inspector of Tong Prefecture was vacant, Can requested appointing Left Vice Director Zhao Jing. Emperor Dezong hated Can and wished to divide his inner circle, and instead appointed Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Household Dou Can favored him and planned to rely on him as successor. When the post of Tong Prefecture inspector fell vacant, Can recommended Left Vice Director Zhao Jing, but Emperor Dezong, who disliked Can, wished to break up his inner circle and instead appointed Lu Zheng.

sentences.zh: 久乃徙華州，厚結權近，冀進用。

translations.literal: After long service he was transferred to Hua Prefecture, thickly cultivating ties with those near power, hoping for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to Hua Prefecture, where he cultivated ties with powerful courtiers in hopes of advancement.

sentences.zh: 同、華地迫而貧，所獻嘗觳陋，至徵厚賦斂，有所奉入，輒加常數，人不堪其求。

translations.literal: Tong and Hua were cramped in territory and poor. What was offered was often meager and shabby. When Zheng arrived he heavily levied taxes. Whenever there was tribute income, he always added to the regular quota. The people could not bear his demands.
translations.idiomatic: Tong and Hua were cramped and poor prefectures whose tribute offerings had been meager, but Lu Zheng imposed heavy levies and always added to the regular quota whenever tribute was delivered, until the people could bear his exactions no longer.

sentences.zh: 若初者，事晏為冗職，包佶稱之。

translations.literal: Ruochu had served Yan in a minor post and was praised by Bao Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruochu had served Liu Yan in a minor post and was praised by Bao Gu.

sentences.zh: 歷太康令，勸刺史李芃斂羨錢，交權幸，芃厚遇之。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Taikang, urged Inspector Li Peng to collect surplus funds, cultivated ties with favorites of power, and Peng treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Taikang, urged the inspector Li Peng to collect surplus funds, cultivated ties with powerful favorites, and was generously treated by Li Peng.

sentences.zh: 累遷浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Observation Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to observation commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 代王緯為浙西觀察、諸道鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: He replaced Wang Wei as Observation Commissioner of Zhexi and Commissioner for Salt and Iron in each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Wang Wei as observation commissioner of Zhexi and commissioner for salt and iron in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 時天下錢少貨輕，州縣禁錢不出境，商賈不通。

translations.literal: At the time cash in the realm was scarce and goods were light in value. Prefectures and counties forbade cash from leaving their borders and merchants could not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time cash was scarce and goods cheap throughout the empire, and prefectures forbade cash from leaving their borders, blocking commerce.

sentences.zh: 若初始奏縱錢以起萬貨，詔可。

translations.literal: Ruochu first memorialized to allow cash to circulate so as to revive ten thousand goods. The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruochu first memorialized to allow cash to circulate freely so as to revive trade, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 而持剛檢下，吏民畏服。

translations.literal: Yet he held to sternness in inspecting subordinates, and officials and people submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he governed with stern discipline, and officials and commoners alike submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 宗經終給事中、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Zongjing ended as Drafting Attendant and Inspector of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjing ended his career as Drafting Attendant and inspector of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子濛，字仁澤。

translations.literal: His son Meng, style name Renze.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Meng, whose style name was Renze.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累官度支郎中。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to Director of the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose to director of the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，擢給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang he was promoted to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huichang reign he was promoted to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以材為宰相李德裕所知。

translations.literal: Because of his talent he was known to the chief minister Li Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: His ability won the notice of Chief Minister Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 時回鶻衰，朝廷經略河、湟，建遣濛按邊，調兵械糧餉，為宣慰靈夏以北党項使。

translations.literal: At the time the Uyghurs were in decline and the court was planning the He and Huang regions. The court dispatched Meng to inspect the frontier, arrange weapons and grain supplies, and made him Commissioner to Console the Tangut tribes north of Ling and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: With the Uyghurs in decline and the court planning operations in the He and Huang regions, Meng was dispatched to inspect the frontier, arrange weapons and grain supplies, and appointed commissioner to console the Tangut tribes north of Ling and Xia.

sentences.zh: 始議造木牛運。

translations.literal: He first proposed constructing wooden oxen for transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first to propose building wooden-ox transport wagons.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，德裕得罪，濛貶朗州刺史，終大理卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended, Li Deyu was found guilty. Meng was demoted to Inspector of Lang Prefecture and ended as Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Li Deyu fell from power and Meng was demoted to inspector of Lang Prefecture, ending his career as director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 晏兄暹，為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Yan's elder brother Xian served as Inspector of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's elder brother Liu Xian served as inspector of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天資疾惡，所至以方直為觀察使所畏。

translations.literal: By nature he was swift to hate evil. Wherever he went, his square uprightness made observation commissioners fear him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was swift to condemn wrongdoing, and wherever he served his uncompromising integrity made observation commissioners fear him.

sentences.zh: 建中末，召為御史大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianzhong he was summoned as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jianzhong reign he was summoned to serve as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 宰相盧杞憚其嚴，更薦前河南尹於頎代之。

translations.literal: The chief minister Lu Qi feared his severity and instead recommended the former Intendant of Henan Yu Yi to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Lu Qi feared his severity and instead recommended the former Henan intendant Yu Yi in his place.

sentences.zh: 暹終潮州刺史。

translations.literal: Xian ended as Inspector of Chao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian ended his career as inspector of Chao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 頎字休明，河南人。

translations.literal: Yi, style name Xiuming, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, whose style name was Xiuming, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 初為京兆士曹參軍，尹史翙器之。

translations.literal: At first he was a Revenue Adjutant of Jingzhao. The intendant Shi Hui valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a revenue adjutant under the Jingzhao intendant, who valued his abilities.

sentences.zh: 翙鎮山南東道，表為判字。

translations.literal: When Hui was posted to Shannan East Circuit, he recommended Yi as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hui was posted to Shannan East Circuit, he recommended Yi as his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 翙死亂兵手，頎挺出收葬之，時稱其誼。

translations.literal: Hui died at the hands of mutinous soldiers. Yi stepped forward to collect and bury him, and at the time his righteousness was praised.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hui was killed by mutinous troops, Yi stepped forward to recover and bury his body, winning praise for his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 累遷京兆尹，任機譎，為政煩碎無大體，元載昵厚之。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Intendant of Jingzhao. He relied on craftiness; his governance was vexatious and petty without broad principles. Yuan Zai was intimate and generous with him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Jingzhao intendant, governing with crafty cleverness in petty, detail-obsessed fashion without grasp of larger principles, and enjoyed the favor of Yuan Zai.

sentences.zh: 載得罪，出鄭州刺史，徙河南尹，以佞柔，故得為大夫。

translations.literal: When Zai was found guilty, he was sent out as Inspector of Zheng Prefecture, transferred to Intendant of Henan, and because of his flattery and softness was able to become Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai fell, Yi was sent out as inspector of Zheng Prefecture, then transferred to Henan intendant, and through flattery and pliancy secured the post of Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三遷工部尚書，入朝，仆金吾仗下，御史劾之，以太子少師致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He was thrice promoted to Minister of Works. Entering court, he fell beneath the Golden Crow guard formation. Censors impeached him. He retired as Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times to Minister of Works. Entering court one day, he fell beneath the Golden Crow guard formation. Censors impeached him, and he retired as Mentor of the Heir Apparent before his death.

sentences.zh: 暹孫潼，字子固。

translations.literal: Xian's grandson Tong, style name Zigù.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian's grandson Liu Tong, whose style name was Zigù.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，杜悰判度支，表為巡官，累遷祠部郎中。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination. When Du Cong judged the Bureau of Revenue, he recommended Tong as touring officer. He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination. When Du Cong took charge of the Bureau of Revenue, he recommended Tong as touring officer, and Tong rose to director of the Bureau of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大中初，討党項羌，軍食乏，宰相欲以潼為使，難其遣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong, when campaigning against the Tangut Qiang, army provisions were scarce. The chief ministers wished to make Tong the envoy but found it hard to dispatch him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong reign, when campaigning against the Tangut Qiang, army provisions ran short. The chief ministers wished to appoint Tong as supply envoy but hesitated to send him.

sentences.zh: 潼見宰相曰：「上念邊饋，議遣使，潼畏不稱耳，安敢憚行？」

translations.literal: Tong met the chief ministers and said: "The emperor is concerned about frontier provisions and discusses sending an envoy. Tong fears only that he may not be equal to the task—how would he dare shrink from going?"
translations.idiomatic: Tong appeared before the chief ministers and said, "The emperor is concerned about frontier supplies and is considering sending an envoy. I fear only that I may not prove equal to the task—how could I shrink from going?"

sentences.zh: 遂命為供軍使。

translations.literal: He was then ordered appointed Army Supply Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly appointed army supply commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會復河、湟，調師屯守，以潼判度支河、湟供軍案。

translations.literal: When the He and Huang regions were recovered, troops were deployed to garrison them, and Tong was made to judge the Bureau of Revenue's He-Huang army supply office.
translations.idiomatic: When the He and Huang regions were recovered and troops deployed to garrison them, Tong was placed in charge of the Bureau of Revenue's He-Huang supply office.

sentences.zh: 歷京兆少尹。

translations.literal: He served as Junior Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He served as junior intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 山南有劇賊，依山為剽，宣宗怒，欲討之，宰相崔鉉曰：「此陛下赤子，迫於饑寒，弄兵山谷間，不足討，請遣使喻釋之。」

translations.literal: In Shannan there were fierce bandits who relied on the mountains for plunder. Emperor Xuanzong was angry and wished to suppress them. The chief minister Cui Xuan said: "These are Your Majesty's own children, driven by hunger and cold to take up arms in the mountain valleys. They are not worth suppressing. Please send an envoy to instruct and release them."
translations.idiomatic: Fierce bandits in Shannan preyed on travelers from mountain strongholds. Emperor Xuanzong was angry and wished to suppress them, but Chief Minister Cui Xuan said, "These are Your Majesty's own children, driven by hunger and cold to take up arms in the valleys. They are not worth a campaign—send an envoy to instruct and release them."

sentences.zh: 詔潼馳往。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tong to hurry there.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Tong to hurry there at once.

sentences.zh: 潼挺身直叩其壘曰：「有詔赦爾罪。」

translations.literal: Tong advanced his body straight to knock on their fortress and said: "There is an edict pardoning your crimes."
translations.idiomatic: Tong went alone to their fortress and announced, "An edict pardons your crimes."

sentences.zh: 盜皆列拜，約潼就館而降。

translations.literal: The bandits all lined up and bowed, agreeing that Tong should come to the lodge and then they would surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits all lined up and bowed, agreeing to surrender once Tong entered their camp.

sentences.zh: 會山南節度使封敖遣兵擊賊，潼罷歸。

translations.literal: Just then the Military Commissioner of Shannan Feng Ao dispatched troops to attack the bandits, and Tong ceased and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Shannan military commissioner Feng Ao dispatched troops to attack the bandits, and Tong withdrew and returned.

sentences.zh: 數陳邊事，擢右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presented frontier affairs and was promoted to Right Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After repeatedly memorializing on frontier affairs, he was promoted to Right Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 出為朔方、靈武節度使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Military Commissioner of Shuofang and Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military commissioner of Shuofang and Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 坐累貶鄭州刺史，改湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Because of implication he was demoted to Inspector of Zheng Prefecture and changed to Observation Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in a case, he was demoted to inspector of Zheng Prefecture, then transferred to observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 召為左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Regular Attendant of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 拜昭義節度使，徙河東，又徙西川。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi, transferred to Hedong, and again transferred to Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of Zhaoyi, then transferred to Hedong and afterward to Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 時李福討南詔，兵不利，潼至，填以恩信，蠻皆如約。

translations.literal: At the time Li Fu was campaigning against Nanzhao and the army fared badly. When Tong arrived, he filled them with favor and trust, and the barbarians all kept their agreements.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fu campaigned against Nanzhao with poor results, Tong arrived and won the tribes over with favor and trust until they all kept their agreements.

sentences.zh: 六姓蠻持兩端，為南詔間候。

translations.literal: The Six-Clan barbarians held to both sides and served as scouts for Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Six-Clan tribes hedged their allegiance and served as scouts for Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 有卑籠部落者請討之，潼因出兵襲擊，俘五千人。

translations.literal: A tribe of the Beilong group requested that they be attacked. Tong accordingly sent troops in a surprise strike and captured five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When the Beilong tribe requested permission to attack them, Tong sent troops in a surprise raid and captured five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 南詔大懼，自是不敢犯邊。

translations.literal: Nanzhao was greatly afraid and from then on did not dare violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao was greatly alarmed and thereafter did not dare raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 以功加檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the additional title of Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was given the additional title of Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 第五琦

translations.literal: Di Wuqi
translations.idiomatic: Di Wuqi

sentences.zh: 第五琦，字禹珪，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Di Wuqi, style name Yugui, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Di Wuqi, whose style name was Yugui, came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少以吏干進，頗能言強國富民術。

translations.literal: In youth he advanced through clerical ability and was quite able to speak of methods to strengthen the state and enrich the people.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he advanced through clerical skill and was adept at expounding methods to strengthen the state and enrich the people.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，事韋堅。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he served Wei Jian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he served under Wei Jian.

sentences.zh: 堅敗，不得調。

translations.literal: When Jian was defeated, he could not be transferred.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Jian fell from power, Wuqi could not secure a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 久之，為須江丞，太守賀蘭進明才之。

translations.literal: After long time he became assistant magistrate of Xujiang. The prefect Helan Jinming valued his talent.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed assistant magistrate of Xujiang, where the prefect Helan Jinming recognized his talent.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，進明徙北海，奏琦為錄事參軍事。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Jinming was transferred to Beihai and memorialized Qi as Recording Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Jinming was transferred to Beihai and recommended Wuqi as recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 時賊已陷河間、信都，進明未戰，玄宗怒，遣使封刀趣之，曰：「不亟進兵，即斬首。」

translations.literal: At the time the rebels had already taken Hejian and Xindu. Jinming had not yet fought. Emperor Xuanzong was angry and dispatched an envoy with a sealed sword to hurry him, saying, "If you do not advance troops at once, your head will be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already seized Hejian and Xindu, yet Jinming had not engaged them. Emperor Xuanzong in anger sent an envoy bearing a sealed sword with the warning, "Advance at once or lose your head.

sentences.zh: 進明懼，不知所出。

translations.literal: Jinming was afraid and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming was terrified and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 琦勸厚以財募勇士，出賊不意。

translations.literal: Qi urged generously using wealth to recruit brave men and strike where the rebels did not expect.
translations.idiomatic: Wuqi urged him to spend generously recruiting brave men and strike where the rebels least expected.

sentences.zh: 如其計，復收所陷郡。

translations.literal: According to his plan, the seized prefectures were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Following his plan, the lost prefectures were recovered.

sentences.zh: 肅宗駐彭原，進明遣琦奏事，既謁見，即陳：「今之急在兵，兵強弱在賦，賦所出以江淮為淵。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong was stationed at Pengyuan. Jinming sent Qi to report affairs. After audience he at once stated: "Today's urgency lies in the army. The army's strength or weakness lies in levies. The source of levies has the Jiang-Huai as its deep pool.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was encamped at Pengyuan. Jinming sent Wuqi to report to court, and upon audience he declared, "The urgent need now is the army; the army's strength depends on revenue; and revenue flows from the Jiang-Huai as from a deep reservoir.

sentences.zh: 若假臣一職，請悉東南寶貲，飛餉函、洛，惟陛下命。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will grant me one post, I request to gather all treasure of the southeast and swiftly supply Hong and Luo—only await Your Majesty's command.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will grant me a post, I shall gather all the southeast's wealth and swiftly supply Hong and Luoyang—only await Your Majesty's command.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，拜監察御史、句當江淮租庸使。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and appointed him Attending Censor and Commissioner for Jiang-Huai Corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and appointed him Attending Censor and commissioner for Jiang-Huai corvée and tax transport.

sentences.zh: 遷司虞員外郎、河南等五道支度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Outside Director of the Bureau of Agriculture and Commissioner for Revenue in five circuits including Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to outside director of the Bureau of Agriculture and revenue commissioner for Henan and four other circuits.

sentences.zh: 遷司金郎中，兼侍御史、諸道鹽鐵鑄錢使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Coinage, concurrently Attending Censor and Commissioner for Salt, Iron, and Coinage in each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Bureau of Coinage and concurrent Attending Censor and commissioner for salt, iron, and coinage in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵名使，自琦始。

translations.literal: The title Commissioner for Salt and Iron began with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The title of salt and iron commissioner began with Wuqi.

sentences.zh: 進度支郎中，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Director of the Bureau of Revenue, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Bureau of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 當軍興，隨事趣辦，人不益賦而用以饒，於是遷戶部侍郎、判度支，河南等道支度、轉運、租庸、鹽鐵、鑄錢、司農、太府出納、山南東西、江西、淮南館驛等使。

translations.literal: During military expansion he handled affairs as they arose. The people were not subjected to added levies yet expenditures were ample. He was therefore transferred to Vice Minister of the Household, judging the Bureau of Revenue, and given charge of revenue, transport, corvée, salt and iron, coinage, the Ministry of Agriculture, the Imperial Storehouse receipts and disbursements, Shannan East and West, Jiangxi, Huainan relay stations, and other commissions.
translations.idiomatic: During the military crisis he handled affairs as they arose so that the people faced no added levies while state funds remained ample. He was therefore promoted to Vice Minister of the Household with charge of the Bureau of Revenue and numerous related commissions.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan he was advanced to Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyuan he was promoted to Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 初，琦請鑄乾元重寶錢，以一代十。

translations.literal: At first Qi requested casting the Qianyuan Heavy Treasure coin, one substituting for ten.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wuqi proposed casting the Qianyuan Heavy Treasure coin, each piece to count as ten.

sentences.zh: 既當國，又鑄重規，一代五十。

translations.literal: Once he held state power, he also cast the Heavy Regulation coin, one substituting for fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held state power, he also cast the Heavy Regulation coin, each piece to count as fifty.

sentences.zh: 會物價騰踴，餓饉相望，議者以為非是，詔貶忠州長史。

translations.literal: When prices soared and famine faced one another, critics said this was wrong, and he was ordered demoted to Chief Administrator of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When prices soared and famine spread, critics condemned the policy and he was demoted to chief administrator of Zhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會有告琦納金者，遣御史馳按，琦辭曰：「位宰相，可自持金邪？

translations.literal: Just then someone reported that Qi had accepted gold. Censors were dispatched to investigate swiftly. Qi said in his defense, "Holding the post of chief minister, how could one carry gold oneself?
