translations.idiomatic: Just then someone reported that Wuqi had accepted bribes in gold. Censors were dispatched to investigate. Wuqi protested, "As chief minister, how could I carry gold on my person?

sentences.zh: 若付受有狀，請歸罪有司。」

translations.literal: If there is proof of giving and receiving, please return guilt to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: If there is proof of bribery, let the responsible office determine my guilt.

sentences.zh: 御史不曉，以為具服，獄上之，遂長流夷州。

translations.literal: The censors did not understand and thought he had confessed. The case was sent up and he was exiled long to Yai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The censors misunderstood this as a confession, sent the case upward, and he was exiled to Yai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，起為朗州刺史，有異政，拜太子賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying he was restored as Inspector of Lang Prefecture. He had unusual governance and was appointed Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Baoying reign he was restored as inspector of Lang Prefecture, where his unusual governance won him appointment as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃盜京師，郭子儀表為糧料使，兼御史大夫、關內元帥副使。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans raided the capital, Guo Ziyi memorialized him as Grain Commissioner, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Guannei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans raided the capital, Guo Ziyi recommended him as grain commissioner and concurrent Censor-in-Chief and deputy commander-in-chief of Guannei.

sentences.zh: 改京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was changed to Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Jingzhao intendant.

sentences.zh: 俄加判度支、鑄錢、鹽鐵、轉運、常平等使。

translations.literal: Shortly he was additionally given charge of the Bureau of Revenue, coinage, salt and iron, transport, and Ever-Normal granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally given charge of the Bureau of Revenue, coinage, salt and iron, transport, and Ever-Normal granaries.

sentences.zh: 累封扶風郡公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 復以戶部侍郎兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: He again served as Vice Minister of the Household concurrently as Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Vice Minister of the Household and concurrent Jingzhao intendant.

sentences.zh: 坐與魚朝恩善，貶括州刺史。

translations.literal: Because of friendship with Yu Chaoen he was demoted to Inspector of Kuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his association with Yu Chaoen he was demoted to inspector of Kuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徙饒、湖二州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Rao and Hu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the prefectures of Rao and Hu.

sentences.zh: 復為太子賓客、東都留守。

translations.literal: He was again made Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Mentor of the Heir Apparent and defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 德宗素聞其才，將復用，召之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong had long heard of his talent and was about to restore him. He was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had long heard of his ability and was about to restore him to office when he was summoned.

sentences.zh: 會卒，年七十一，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: Just then he died, age seventy-one, posthumously given Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died before taking office, at age seventy-one, and was posthumously appointed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子峰、婦鄭，皆以孝著，表闕於門。

translations.literal: His sons Feng and his daughter-in-law the Lady Zheng were all famed for filial piety, and a memorial tablet was set up at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng and his daughter-in-law Lady Zheng were all famed for filial piety, and a memorial tablet was erected at their gate.

sentences.zh: 班宏，衛州汲人。

translations.literal: Ban Hong was a native of Ji in Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Hong came from Ji in Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父景倩，國子祭酒，以儒名家。

translations.literal: His father Jingqian was Rector of the Directorate of Education and made the family famous through Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ban Jingqian was Rector of the Directorate of Education and made the family renowned through Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 宏，天寶中擢進士第，調右司禦胄曹參軍。

translations.literal: Hong, in the Tianbao era, passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Right Assistant in the Bureau of Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign Hong passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant in the Bureau of Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 高適鎮劍南，表為觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Gao Shi was posted to Jiannan, he recommended Hong as observation administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Shi was posted to Jiannan, he recommended Hong as his observation administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 青城人以左道惑眾，謀作亂。

translations.literal: People of Qingcheng used heterodox ways to delude the masses and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qingcheng used heterodox teachings to delude the masses and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事覺，誣引屯將規緩死，眾兇懼，宏驗治，即殺之，人心大安。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, they falsely implicated garrison generals in a plot to delay execution. The ringleaders were afraid. Hong verified and judged the case and at once executed them. The people's hearts were greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, the ringleaders falsely implicated garrison officers to delay execution. Hong investigated, immediately executed the guilty, and greatly reassured the people.

sentences.zh: 郭英乂代適，表雒令，以病解。

translations.literal: Guo Yingyi replaced Gao Shi and recommended him as magistrate of Luo, but he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yingyi succeeded Gao Shi and recommended him as magistrate of Luo, but Hong resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，擢起居舍人，四遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat and four times advanced to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign he was promoted to Secretariat attendant and advanced four times to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 李寶臣死，子惟嶽匿喪求節度，帝遣宏使成德喻其軍，惟嶽厚獻遣，宏不納，還報稱旨，擢刑部侍郎、京官考使。

translations.literal: When Li Baochen died, his son Wei Yue concealed the death and sought the military commission. The emperor dispatched Hong to Chengde to instruct the army. Wei Yue richly offered gifts for his departure, but Hong did not accept them. His return report accorded with the imperial intent, and he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Commissioner for Capital Official Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baochen died, his son Li Wei Yue concealed the death and sought the military commission. The emperor dispatched Hong to instruct the Chengde army. Wei Yue offered lavish parting gifts, but Hong refused them. His report pleased the throne, and he was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and commissioner for capital official evaluation.

sentences.zh: 右僕射崔寧署兵部侍郎劉乃為上下考，宏不從，曰：「今軍在節度，雖有尺籍伍符，省署不校也。

translations.literal: The Right Vice Director Cui Ning assigned Vice Minister of War Liu Nai for highest and lowest evaluation. Hong did not agree and said, "Today the army is under the military commission. Though there are roster rolls and tally tallies, the central offices do not verify them.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Cui Ning assigned Vice Minister of War Liu Nai the highest and lowest evaluation grades. Hong refused, saying, "The armies now lie under military commissioners. Though roster rolls exist, the central offices do not verify them.

sentences.zh: 夫上多虛美，則下趨競；

translations.literal: When superiors are full of empty praise, then subordinates rush to compete;
translations.idiomatic: When superiors heap empty praise upon subordinates, inferiors rush to compete;

sentences.zh: 上阿容，則下朋黨。」

translations.literal: when superiors indulge favor, then subordinates form factions.
translations.idiomatic: when superiors indulge flattery, inferiors form factions.

sentences.zh: 因削之。

translations.literal: He therefore struck it out.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore struck the evaluation from the record.

sentences.zh: 乃聞，謝曰：「敢掠一美以邀二罪乎？」

translations.literal: When Nai heard, he apologized and said, "How would I dare seize one praise to invite two crimes?
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Nai heard, he apologized, "How could I seize one compliment only to invite two punishments?

sentences.zh: 進吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was promoted to Vice Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，仍旱蝗，賦調益急，以戶部侍郎副度支使韓滉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, drought and locusts continued and tax levies grew ever more urgent. He served as Vice Minister of the Household assisting the revenue commissioner Han Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan reign, drought and locusts persisted and tax levies grew urgent. He served as Vice Minister of the Household assisting revenue commissioner Han Huang.

sentences.zh: 俄而竇參當國，代滉使。

translations.literal: Shortly Dou Can held state power and replaced Huang as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dou Can took power and replaced Huang as revenue commissioner.

sentences.zh: 而參任大理司直時，宏已為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Can had served as Director of Justice, Hong was already Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can had served as director of justice, Hong was already Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 德宗以宏熟天下計，故進宏尚書副參，且曰：「朕藉宰相重，而眾務一委卿，無庸辭。」

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong, because Hong was versed in the realm's accounts, therefore advanced Hong as Minister assisting Can, and moreover said, "I rely on the chief minister's weight, yet entrust all affairs to you—do not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hong knew the empire's finances thoroughly, Dezong promoted him to Minister assisting Dou Can, saying, "I rely on my chief minister's authority, yet entrust all fiscal affairs to you—do not decline.

sentences.zh: 參亦以宏素貴，私謂曰：「閱歲當歸使於公。」

translations.literal: Can also, because Hong had long been noble, privately told him, "After a year I shall return the commission to you."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can, knowing Hong's long-standing prestige, privately told him, "After a year I shall return the commission to you."

sentences.zh: 宏喜。

translations.literal: Hong was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was pleased.

sentences.zh: 後參胖自安，不念前語。

translations.literal: Later Can grew fat and self-assured and did not remember his earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: Later Dou Can grew complacent and forgot his promise.

sentences.zh: 宏剛愎，以參欺己，議事稍不合。

translations.literal: Hong was obstinate and proud. Because Can deceived him, their deliberations gradually disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was obstinate and proud. Feeling deceived by Dou Can, he increasingly disagreed with him in council.

sentences.zh: 揚子院，鹽鐵轉運之委藏也，宏任御史中丞徐粲主之，粲以賄聞，參議所代，宏固不可。

translations.literal: The Yangzi Depot was the entrusted storehouse of salt and iron transport. Hong had Attending Censor-in-Chief Xu Can manage it. Can was known for bribery. Can deliberated on a replacement, but Hong firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi depot was the entrusted storehouse for salt and iron transport. Hong had Attending Censor-in-Chief Xu Can manage it. When Xu Can's bribery became known and Dou Can sought a replacement, Hong firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 參選諸院吏，未始訪宏，宏數條參所用吏過惡以聞，輒留中。

translations.literal: Can selected clerks from the various offices without ever consulting Hong. Hong repeatedly listed the faults of Can's chosen clerks and reported them, but they were always held within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can selected clerks from various offices without consulting Hong, who repeatedly reported the faults of Can's appointees, but the memorials were always held within the palace.

sentences.zh: 無何，參以使勞，加吏部尚書，而封宏蕭國公。

translations.literal: Before long, Can because of commission labors was given additional title Minister of the Civil Service, while Hong was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dou Can was given the additional title Minister of the Civil Service for his labors, while Hong was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 恨參以虛寵加己，銜之。

translations.literal: He resented that Can had added empty honors to him and bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Hong resented that Dou Can had heaped empty honors upon him and nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 每制旨有所營建，必極瑰麗，親程役，媚結權嬖以傾參。

translations.literal: Whenever imperial orders involved construction, he always made them extremely magnificent, personally supervised the labor, and curried favor with powerful favorites to overturn Can.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever imperial orders involved construction, he made the projects extravagantly magnificent, personally supervised the labor, and curried favor with powerful favorites to undermine Dou Can.

sentences.zh: 張滂先善於宏，薦為司農少卿。

translations.literal: Zhang Pang had first been friendly with Hong and recommended him as Vice Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang had first been friendly with Hong and recommended him as Vice Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 及參欲滂分掌江、淮鹽鐵，宏以滂疾惡，且以法繩粲，因謬曰：「滂強戾不可用。」

translations.literal: When Can wished Pang to share management of Jiang-Huai salt and iron, Hong, because Pang was harsh and evil and because he used the law to bind Can, therefore falsely said, "Pang is violent and obstinate and cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can wished Zhang Pang to share management of Jiang-Huai salt and iron, Hong—because Pang was harsh and because Hong had used the law against Xu Can—falsely declared, "Pang is violent and obstinate and cannot be used.

sentences.zh: 滂聞，不喜。

translations.literal: When Pang heard, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Pang heard, he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 久之，參知帝遇己薄，乃讓使，然不欲宏專，問策於京兆尹薛玨，玨曰：「滂與宏交惡，而滂剛決。

translations.literal: After long time, Can knew the emperor's regard for him had grown thin. He therefore yielded the commission, yet did not wish Hong to monopolize it. He asked strategy of the Intendant of Jingzhao Xue Jue. Jue said, "Pang and Hong are mutually hostile, and Pang is firm and decisive.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Dou Can knew the emperor's regard for him had waned. He yielded the commission yet did not wish Hong to monopolize it, and asked strategy of Jingzhao intendant Xue Jue, who said, "Pang and Hong are enemies, and Pang is firm and decisive.

sentences.zh: 若分鹽鐵轉運，必能制宏。」

translations.literal: If salt and iron transport is divided, he will surely be able to control Hong.
translations.idiomatic: If salt and iron transport is divided, he will surely be able to control Hong.

sentences.zh: 參遂薦滂為戶部侍郎、鹽鐵轉運使，而以宏判度支，分滂關內、河東、劍南、山南西道鹽鐵轉運隸宏，以悅其意。

translations.literal: Can therefore recommended Pang as Vice Minister of the Household and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport, while Hong judged the Bureau of Revenue. Pang's Guannei, Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan West salt and iron transport was placed under Hong to please him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can therefore recommended Zhang Pang as Vice Minister of the Household and salt and iron transport commissioner, while Hong retained charge of the Bureau of Revenue. Pang's jurisdiction over Guannei, Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan West was placed under Hong to appease him.

sentences.zh: 又還江淮兩稅，置巡院官，令宏、滂共差擇。

translations.literal: The two-tax system of Jiang-Huai was also restored, and touring depot officials were established, with Hong and Pang jointly selecting them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Huai two-tax system was restored and touring depot officials established, to be jointly selected by Hong and Pang.

sentences.zh: 滂欲得簿最，宏不與。

translations.literal: Pang wished to obtain the account registers, but Hong would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang wished to obtain the account registers, but Hong refused.

sentences.zh: 及署院官，更持可否不能定，處處官乏不補。

translations.literal: When appointing depot officials, they again held to approval or disapproval and could not decide. Everywhere offices lacked staff and were not filled.
translations.idiomatic: When appointing depot officials, the two men could not agree, and offices everywhere went unfilled.

sentences.zh: 滂奏言：「臣職不修，無逃死，如國家大計何？」

translations.literal: Pang memorialized, saying, "Your servant's duties are not properly performed and cannot escape death—but what of the state's great plans?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang memorialized, "Your servant has failed in his duties and deserves death—but what of the state's great plans?

sentences.zh: 由是有詔分掌。

translations.literal: Because of this there was an edict for divided management.
translations.idiomatic: An edict therefore ordered divided management.

sentences.zh: 宏見宰相辭曰：「宏主漕，歲得江、淮米五十萬斛，前年至七十萬。

translations.literal: Hong met the chief ministers and resigned, saying, "Hong managed transport and annually obtained five hundred thousand hu of Jiang-Huai grain. The year before last it reached seven hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Hong appeared before the chief ministers and offered to resign, saying, "I managed transport and annually delivered five hundred thousand hu of Jiang-Huai grain, reaching seven hundred thousand the year before last.

sentences.zh: 今職移於人，敢請罪。」

translations.literal: Now the duty has shifted to another. I dare request punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Now the duty has passed to another. I dare request punishment.

sentences.zh: 滂在側儳曰：「公所言非也。

translations.literal: Pang, standing at his side, suddenly said, "What you say is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pang, standing beside him, suddenly interjected, "What you say is not so.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不奪公職，乃公喪官緡，縱奸吏，自取咎爾。

translations.literal: The court did not strip you of your office. You yourself lost control of revenue strings, indulged corrupt clerks, and invited blame on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not strip you of office. You yourself lost control of revenue, indulged corrupt clerks, and brought blame upon yourself.

sentences.zh: 凡為度支使，不一歲家輒鉅億，僮馬產第侈王公，非盜縣官財何以然？

translations.literal: Whoever serves as revenue commissioner, within a year his household amasses hundreds of millions. Servants, horses, estates, and mansions rival those of kings and dukes. How could this be unless he stole official wealth?
translations.idiomatic: Every revenue commissioner, within a year, amasses hundreds of millions at home. Servants, horses, estates, and mansions rival those of kings and dukes. How could this happen except by stealing official wealth?

sentences.zh: 上既知之，故令滂分掌。

translations.literal: The emperor already knows this, and therefore ordered Pang to share management.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already knows this, and therefore ordered me to share management.

sentences.zh: 今公無乃歸怨上乎？」

translations.literal: Now will you not shift blame to the emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you now shift blame to the emperor?"

sentences.zh: 宏不答，於是移病歸第。

translations.literal: Hong did not answer and therefore reported illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Hong made no reply and reported illness, returning home.

sentences.zh: 宰相白其狀，詔許如劉晏、韓滉故事，以東都、河南、淮南、江南、山南東道兩稅，滂主之，東渭橋以東巡院隸焉；

translations.literal: The chief ministers reported the situation. An edict permitted following the precedents of Liu Yan and Han Huang. The two taxes of the Eastern Capital, Henan, Huainan, Jiangnan, and Shannan East Circuit were managed by Pang, and touring depots east of the Eastern Wei Bridge were subordinate to him;
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers reported the situation. An edict followed the precedents of Liu Yan and Han Huang: Zhang Pang took charge of the two-tax system for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Huainan, Jiangnan, and Shannan East Circuit, with touring depots east of the Eastern Wei Bridge subordinate to him;

sentences.zh: 關內、河東、劍南、山南西道宏主之。

translations.literal: Guannei, Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan West Circuit were managed by Hong.
translations.idiomatic: while Hong took charge of Guannei, Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 滂至揚州，乃窮劾粲，悉發其贓至鉅萬，徙死嶺表。

translations.literal: When Pang reached Yangzhou, he thoroughly impeached Can, fully exposing his bribes to tens of thousands, and Can was banished to die in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Pang reached Yangzhou, he thoroughly impeached Xu Can, exposing bribes worth tens of thousands, and Can was banished to die in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 宏清潔勤力，晨入官署夕而出，吏不堪其勞，而己益恭。

translations.literal: Hong was pure, diligent, and forceful. He entered the office at dawn and left at dusk. Clerks could not bear the labor, yet he himself grew ever more respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was pure, diligent, and tireless. He entered the office at dawn and left at dusk. Clerks could scarcely bear the labor, yet he himself grew ever more respectful.

sentences.zh: 參得罪，宏為有力。

translations.literal: When Can was found guilty, Hong had been a powerful factor.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can fell, Hong had been instrumental.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: When he died, age seventy-three, he was posthumously given Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age seventy-three and was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 後二年，滂亦罷為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: Two years later Pang was also removed and made Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Zhang Pang was also removed and made director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 王紹，本名純，避憲宗諱改焉。

translations.literal: Wang Shao, original name Chun, changed to avoid the taboo of Emperor Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao, whose original name was Chun, changed it to avoid the taboo of Emperor Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 自太原徙京兆之萬年。

translations.literal: His family moved from Taiyuan to Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His family moved from Taiyuan to Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父端，第進士，有名天寶間，與柳芳、陸據、殷寅友善。

translations.literal: His father Duan passed the jinshi examination and was famous in the Tianbao era, friendly with Liu Fang, Lu Ju, and Yin Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Duan passed the jinshi examination and was famed during the Tianbao reign, counting Liu Fang, Lu Ju, and Yin Yin among his friends.

sentences.zh: 據嘗言：「端之莊，芳之辯，寅之介，可以名世。」

translations.literal: Ju once said: "Duan's dignity, Fang's eloquence, and Yin's integrity can make names in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ju once remarked, "Duan's dignity, Fang's eloquence, and Yin's integrity can make names in the world.

sentences.zh: 終工部員外郎。

translations.literal: He ended as Outside Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duan ended his career as outside director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 紹少為顏真卿所器，字之曰德素，奏為武康尉。

translations.literal: Shao in youth was valued by Yan Zhenqing, who gave him the style name Desu and memorialized him as Commandant of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Shao won the esteem of Yan Zhenqing, who gave him the style name Desu and recommended him as commandant of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 再佐蕭復府。

translations.literal: He twice served as aide in Xiao Fu's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He twice served as aide on Xiao Fu's staff.

sentences.zh: 包佶領租庸、鹽鐵使，署判官。

translations.literal: When Bao Gu held the corvée and salt and iron commissions, he appointed him administrative judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao Gu held the corvée and salt and iron commissions, he appointed Shao as his administrative judge.

sentences.zh: 時李希烈阻兵江淮，輸物留梗，乃徙餉道自潁入汴。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xiyan blocked the Jiang-Huai with troops and transport goods were detained. He therefore shifted the supply route from Ying into Bian.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Xiyan blocked the Jiang-Huai with troops and transport goods were detained, so Shao shifted the supply route from Ying into Bian.

sentences.zh: 紹及關，德宗已西狩，乃督輕貨趣間道走洋州。

translations.literal: When Shao reached the pass, Dezong had already gone west on hunt. He therefore supervised light goods and hurried by bypath to Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao reached Tong Pass, Dezong had already fled west. He therefore drove light goods along back roads to Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹先見行在，帝勞之曰：「吾軍乏春服，朕且衣裘，奈何？」

translations.literal: Shao first saw the mobile court. The emperor consoled him and said: "Our army lacks spring clothing. I myself am wearing furs—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao was the first to reach the mobile court. The emperor greeted him with concern: "Our army lacks spring clothing, and I myself am still wearing furs—what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 紹流涕曰：「佶遣臣貢奉，無慮五十萬，當即至。」

translations.literal: Shao wept and said: "Gu dispatched your servant with tribute. No less than five hundred thousand— it should arrive at once."
translations.idiomatic: Shao wept and said, "Bao Gu sent me with tribute—no less than five hundred thousand pieces—and it should arrive at once."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「道回遠，經費方急，何可望邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The road is circuitous and far. Expenditures are just now urgent—how can there be hope?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The road is long and circuitous, and funds are desperately short—how can we hope for that?"

sentences.zh: 後五日繼至，由是紓難。

translations.literal: Five days later it arrived in succession, and thereby difficulty was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later the goods arrived in succession, and the crisis was relieved.

sentences.zh: 遷倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Outside Director of the Bureau of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to outside director of the Bureau of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 是時，兵旱無年，詔戶部收闕官俸、稅茶及無名錢，以修荒政。

translations.literal: At the time, warfare and drought left no good year. An edict ordered the Household Ministry to collect vacant official salaries, tea taxes, and unnamed levies to repair famine governance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time warfare and drought brought year after year of hardship. An edict ordered the Ministry of the Household to collect vacant official salaries, tea taxes, and miscellaneous levies to fund famine relief.

sentences.zh: 紹由員外郎判務，遷戶部、兵部郎中，皆專領。

translations.literal: Shao from Outside Director judged affairs and was transferred to Director of the Household and War ministries, all with sole charge.
translations.idiomatic: Shao advanced from outside director to director of the Household and War ministries, holding sole charge of each.

sentences.zh: 進戶部侍郎，判度支，頃之遷尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of the Household, judging the Bureau of Revenue, and shortly transferred to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Household with charge of the Bureau of Revenue and shortly thereafter to Minister.

sentences.zh: 德宗臨禦久，益不假借宰相，自竇參、陸贄斥罷，中書取充位，惟紹謹密，眷待殊厚。

translations.literal: Dezong had long held the throne and increasingly did not lend authority to chief ministers. Since Dou Can and Lu Zhi were dismissed and expelled, the Secretariat took men merely to fill posts. Only Shao was careful and secretive, receiving exceptionally thick favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had long held the throne and increasingly withheld authority from chief ministers. After Dou Can and Lu Zhi were dismissed, the Secretariat was filled with placeholders. Only Shao, careful and discreet, received exceptionally generous favor.

sentences.zh: 主計凡八年，每政事多所關訪，紹亦未嘗一言漏於人。

translations.literal: He managed accounts for eight years in all. Whenever state affairs were involved he was consulted, yet Shao never let a single word leak to others.
translations.idiomatic: He managed state accounts for eight years. Whenever affairs of state arose the emperor consulted him, yet Shao never let a single word leak to outsiders.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，王叔文奪其權，拜兵部尚書，出為東都留守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong ascended, Wang Shuwen seized his authority. He was appointed Minister of War and sent out as Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong took the throne, Wang Shuwen stripped him of his authority. He was appointed Minister of War and sent out as defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 元和初，檢校尚書右僕射，為武寧軍節度使，復以濠、泗二州隸其軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army. Hao and Si prefectures were again placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and military commissioner of the Wuning army, with Hao and Si prefectures again placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 自張愔後，兵驕難治，紹搜輯軍政，推誠示人，裨將安進達、唐重靖謀亂，紹以計取之，出家貲賞士，舉軍安賴。

translations.literal: After Zhang Yin, the troops were arrogant and hard to govern. Shao gathered and ordered military affairs, showing sincerity to men. The deputy generals An Jinda and Tang Chongjing plotted rebellion. Shao used stratagem to capture them, spent family wealth to reward soldiers, and the whole army settled in reliance.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yin the troops had grown arrogant and unruly. Shao reorganized military affairs and won men over with sincerity. When deputy generals An Jinda and Tang Chongjing plotted rebellion, Shao outmaneuvered them, spent his own fortune rewarding the troops, and the whole army settled into loyalty.

sentences.zh: 復拜兵部尚書，判戶部。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Minister of War, judging the Household Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Minister of War with charge of the Ministry of the Household.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈右僕射，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: When he died, age seventy-two, he was posthumously given Right Vice Director, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age seventy-two and was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 李巽，字令叔，趙州贊皇人。

translations.literal: Li Xun, style name Lingshu, was a native of Zanhuang in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, whose style name was Lingshu, came from Zanhuang in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以明經補華州參軍事，舉拔萃，授鄠尉。

translations.literal: Through the Mingjing examination he was appointed Military Adjutant of Hua Prefecture. Recommended through the Baocui selection, he was given the post of Commandant of E.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Mingjing examination he was appointed military adjutant of Hua Prefecture, then through the Baocui selection was made commandant of E.

sentences.zh: 進累左司郎中、常州刺史，召拜給事中，出為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: He was advanced and accumulated posts as Director of the Left Secretariat and Inspector of Chang Prefecture. He was summoned and appointed Drafting Attendant, then sent out as Observation Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of director of the Left Secretariat and inspector of Chang Prefecture, was summoned as Drafting Attendant, and was sent out as observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，徙江西。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan he was transferred to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan he was transferred to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 巽銳於為治，持下以法，察無遺私，吏不敢少紿。

translations.literal: Xun was sharp in governance, holding subordinates by law, investigating without leaving private matters, and officials did not dare slight deception.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was sharp in governance, ruling subordinates by law and investigating without favoritism, so that officials dared not deceive him in the slightest.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，擢兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong took the throne, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 杜佑表為鹽鐵、轉運副使，俄代佑。

translations.literal: Du You memorialized him as Deputy Commissioner for Salt, Iron, and Transport, and shortly he replaced You.
translations.idiomatic: Du You recommended him as deputy commissioner for salt, iron, and transport, and he shortly succeeded Du You.

sentences.zh: 使任自劉晏後，職廢不振，賦入朘耗。

translations.literal: Since Liu Yan's time the commissioner's duty had languished without revival and tax revenue had dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Yan's time the transport commission had languished and tax revenue had dwindled.

sentences.zh: 巽蒞職一年，較所入如晏最多之年，明年過之，又明年，增百八十萬緡。

translations.literal: In one year of Xun's holding office, revenue compared to Yan's highest year; the next year it surpassed it; and the year after that it increased by 1.8 million strings.
translations.idiomatic: In his first year in office revenue matched Liu Yan's best year; the next year it surpassed it; and the year after that it increased by 1.8 million strings.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 天資長於吏事，至治家，亦句檢案牘簿書如公府。

translations.literal: By nature he excelled in clerical affairs. Even in managing the household he scrutinized documents and account books like a public office.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he excelled in administrative affairs. Even in managing his household he scrutinized documents and account books as rigorously as a government office.

sentences.zh: 史有過，秋毫無所縱，股栗脅息，常如與巽對。

translations.literal: When clerks had faults, not an autumn hair was spared. Thighs trembled and breath was held in fear, as if constantly facing Xun.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks erred, he spared not the slightest fault. They trembled in fear as if constantly standing before him.

sentences.zh: 程異坐王叔文廢，巽特薦引之。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi was dismissed because of Wang Shuwen. Xun specially recommended and introduced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Yi was dismissed because of Wang Shuwen, Xun specially recommended and brought him forward.

sentences.zh: 異之計較精於巽，故巽能善職，蓋有助雲。

translations.literal: Yi's calculations were more precise than Xun's. Therefore Xun could perform his duties well—likely he had help.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi's calculations were more precise than Xun's own, so that Xun could perform his duties well—likely with his assistance.

sentences.zh: 元和四年疾革，郎官省候，巽言不及病，但與商校程課功利。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe his illness became critical. Court officials came to inquire. Xun spoke not of illness but only discussed and verified schedules, tasks, and profit and loss.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhe his illness became critical. Court officials came to inquire after him, but Xun spoke not of his illness—only of schedules, tasks, and profit and loss.

sentences.zh: 是夕卒，年六十三，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: That evening he died, age sixty-three, posthumously given Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he died, at age sixty-three, and was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 巽為人忌刻校怨，在江西，有所憎恨輒殺之。

translations.literal: Xun as a man was jealous, harsh, and exacting in grudges. In Jiangxi, whomever he hated he at once killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was jealous, harsh, and exacting in his grudges. In Jiangxi he killed whomever he hated.

sentences.zh: 始，竇參為相，出巽常州，促其行。

translations.literal: At first, when Dou Can was chief minister, he sent Xun out to Chang Prefecture and urged his departure.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Dou Can was chief minister, he sent Xun out to Chang Prefecture and urged him to depart quickly.

sentences.zh: 及參貶郴州，巽時觀察湖南，宣武節度使劉士寧致絹數千匹於參，巽即劾參交通藩鎮，以怒德宗，遂殺參雲。

translations.literal: When Can was demoted to Chen Prefecture, Xun was then Observation Commissioner of Hunan. The Military Commissioner of Xuanwu Liu Shining sent several thousand bolts of silk to Can. Xun at once impeached Can for communicating with military commissioners, enraging Dezong, and thus Can was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can was demoted to Chen Prefecture, Xun was observation commissioner of Hunan. The Xuanwu military commissioner Liu Shining sent several thousand bolts of silk to Can, and Xun immediately impeached Can for communicating with military commissioners, enraging Dezong and leading to Can's execution.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：生人之本，食與貨而已。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The root of sustaining the people is only food and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: The foundation of sustaining the people is food and goods alone.

sentences.zh: 知所以取，人不怨；

translations.literal: Know how to take, and the people do not resent;
translations.idiomatic: Know how to take, and the people do not resent it;

sentences.zh: 知所以予，人不乏。

translations.literal: know how to give, and the people are not in want.
translations.idiomatic: know how to give, and the people are not left in want.

sentences.zh: 道禦之而王，權用之而霸，古今一也。

translations.literal: The Way governs it and one becomes king; power employs it and one becomes hegemon—the same in ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: Govern it by the Way and one becomes king; wield it by power and one becomes hegemon—the principle is the same in every age.

sentences.zh: 劉晏因平準法，斡山海，排商賈，制萬物低昂，常操天下贏貲，以佐軍興。

translations.literal: Liu Yan through the Ever-Normal method turned mountains and seas, excluded merchants, controlled the rise and fall of ten thousand goods, constantly held the realm's profitable wealth, and thereby assisted military expansion.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan applied the Ever-Normal method to turn mountains and seas to account, curb merchants, regulate the prices of all goods, and constantly command the empire's profitable wealth to fund the armies.

sentences.zh: 雖拿兵數十年，斂不及民而用度足。

translations.literal: Though wielding armies for several decades, levies did not reach the people yet expenditures were sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Though the empire waged war for decades, levies did not crush the people yet state expenditures remained ample.

sentences.zh: 唐中僨而振，晏有勞焉，可謂知取予矣。

translations.literal: Mid-Tang declined yet revived—Yan had merit in this and may be called one who knew how to take and give.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Tang declined yet revived, and Yan had no small share in that revival—he may truly be said to have known how to take and how to give.

sentences.zh: 其經晏辟署者，皆用材顯，循其法，亦能富國雲。

translations.literal: Those who passed through Yan's recruitment and appointment all used their talents to become prominent. Following his methods, they too could enrich the state.
translations.idiomatic: Those whom Yan recruited and appointed all rose to prominence through their talents, and by following his methods they too could enrich the state.
